around.headline: Man hacked to death by bike-borne attackers at a Bengaluru traffic signal near Madiwala
around.summary: A man was fatally attacked with swords by bike-borne assailants during a traffic jam near Madiwala, and police teams are hunting the attackers, per today's reports. If a violent altercation breaks out near you in traffic, stay in your vehicle with doors locked and call 112 rather than stepping out to intervene.

around.headline: Bengaluru Metro's full airport connectivity now pushed to March 2028
around.summary: The Blue Line to Kempegowda International Airport will open in phases from mid-2027, with full connectivity only by March 2028, the minister said, while separate data shows signalling, power and train faults disrupted the metro 15 times in the last 10 months. If you rely on the airport line for travel, keep budgeting extra buffer time or a backup route for at least another 18 months.

around.headline: KPSC exam scam: ED raids premises of 'missing' IAS officer Gyanendra Gangwar
around.summary: The ED raided the Bengaluru and Bareilly premises of IAS officer Gyanendra Gangwar, who had gone incommunicado after his flight landed, in connection with the KPSC recruitment exam scam; the home minister later said he's safe in his hometown, per today's reports. A reminder that even senior officials get pulled into exam-paper and recruitment scams — treat any 'guaranteed selection' offer for government exams as a red flag.
around.source: The Times of India, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Karnataka H1N1 cases cross 4,000, government to take stock
around.summary: Karnataka's H1N1 flu case count has crossed 4,000 statewide, prompting the government to review the response, per today's report — this follows the recent Bengaluru school outbreak. Watch for fever, body ache and cough in yourself or family, and don't delay a doctor visit if symptoms persist beyond 2-3 days.

around.headline: Consumer court orders firm to pay Rs 5,000 after number plate arrives a year late
around.summary: A Bengaluru consumer court ordered a company to pay Rs 5,000 in compensation to a customer whose vehicle number plate arrived a full year after it was ordered, per today's report. Small, unreasonable delays from vendors are worth escalating — district consumer forums handle claims like this without needing a lawyer.

around.headline: Expired drug bust in Karnataka: doctors flag risks that go beyond the printed date
around.summary: Following a recent expired-medicine seizure in Karnataka, doctors are warning that expired drugs can lose potency or turn harmful well before or after the printed date depending on storage, per today's report. Always check the expiry date on strips yourself when buying medicines, especially from smaller or roadside chemists.

street_smart.title: You're paying the bill at a Bengaluru cafe and notice the item description reads something like "little fat black shirt" instead of what you ordered — a humiliating remark about your appearance printed right on the receipt. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real incident: a Bengaluru cafe faced backlash after a customer's bill described them by a body-shaming remark instead of their order, and the company later apologised (The Times of India, NDTV, India Today). This is a fresh angle not covered as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: You're at the counter, other customers are around, and staff seem unbothered — like this is normal shorthand for them.

choices.text: Photograph the bill as evidence, calmly ask to speak to the manager on the spot, and if it isn't resolved, file a complaint with the National Consumer Helpline (1800-11-4000) or via the e-daakhil portal.
choices.feedback: Correct — documenting the bill first gives you proof that can't be disputed later, and raising it with the manager gives the business a chance to fix it immediately. If they brush you off, the consumer helpline and e-daakhil portal exist exactly for discriminatory or unprofessional service like this, and having photo evidence makes that complaint far stronger.

choices.text: Post a photo of the bill on social media immediately, tagging the cafe, before saying anything to staff.
choices.feedback: Public pressure can work fast, as it did here, but going public before giving the business a chance to respond raises your own legal exposure if any detail is later disputed. Documenting first and posting afterward — if the manager doesn't act — protects you better and still gets results.

choices.text: Raise your voice, refuse to pay, and demand the staff member be fired right there.
choices.feedback: This is the trap — a loud confrontation can escalate into the establishment calling it a payment dispute or public nuisance against you, muddying who was actually in the wrong. It also gives them no paper trail to act on afterward, so nothing changes structurally.

choices.text: Feel embarrassed, pay quietly, and just avoid that cafe in future.
choices.feedback: Understandable, but it lets the behaviour continue for the next customer and leaves you with no record if it happens again elsewhere. A quiet photo and a polite word to the manager cost you almost nothing extra and can actually get it fixed.

takeaways: Photograph any offensive or wrongly itemised bill immediately — in written-record disputes, it's often the only evidence that holds up.
The National Consumer Helpline (1800-11-4000) and the e-daakhil online portal both accept complaints about rude or discriminatory service, not just faulty products.
Documenting first and escalating publicly only if unresolved gets faster real action and protects you legally, compared to going public in the heat of the moment.

quiz.why: The line will open in phases starting mid-2027, but full airport connectivity is targeted only for March 2028.

quiz.why: H1N1 is a seasonal flu strain — most cases resolve with rest and fluids, but the very young, elderly, and those with existing conditions face higher risk and should see a doctor early.

quiz.question: In banking, the "repo rate" is the rate at which:
options: Banks lend to each other overnight
The RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
Banks charge customers on credit cards
The government borrows from the public via bonds
quiz.why: When the RBI raises the repo rate, borrowing gets costlier for banks, which usually pass it on as higher loan and EMI rates for consumers.

quiz.question: Which constitutional amendment lowered India's voting age from 21 to 18?
quiz.why: The 61st Amendment, passed in 1988, took effect in 1989 and brought millions of young first-time voters into the electorate.
